title: Examining Australia's Move on Social Media Ban for Those Aged 16 and Below
what_it_is: Examining Australia's Move on Social Media Ban for Those Aged 16 and Below

sections.label: Age limits for social media
sections.summary: The objective of legislating age limits for social media access is to protect children and youths from its harms, and effectiveness will continue to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The stated objective of legislating age limits for social media access is to protect children and youths from its harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We share the same objective and will continue to study the effectiveness of mandating age limits.

sections.label: Code of Practice for Online Safety
sections.summary: In 2023, the Code of Practice for Online Safety was introduced.

sentences.text: In 2023, we introduced the Code of Practice for Online Safety.

sections.label: Age assurance and app stores
sections.summary: Restrictive account settings and parental tools are required, and the upcoming Code of Practice for Online Safety for App Distribution Services will require designated app stores to implement age assurance measures.

sentences.text: They must also have more restrictive account settings for children and provide tools for parents to manage their safety.

We have also taken decisive steps to require the implementation of age assurance methods, which have grown in availability and effectiveness, and can help to minimise children’s access to harmful online content.

Our upcoming Code of Practice for Online Safety for App Distribution Services will require designated app stores to put in place such measures to ensure that children access only apps that are appropriate for their age.

sections.label: Annual online report transparency
sections.summary: The intent of requiring designated social media services to submit annual online reports is to provide transparency on their measures and safety levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On the first bucket of questions that she raised relating to the designated social media services, indeed, the whole intent of having them submit the annual online report is to provide transparency on their measures and levels of safety to see what they are already doing in the space and also help us to understand what are some of the features that can be put in place to provide the safeguards.

sections.label: Positive Use Guide on Technology
sections.summary: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information will introduce a Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media in the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: My Ministry, the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, will also introduce a Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media in the first half of this year.

sections.label: Online Safety Code compliance penalties
sections.summary: The Online Safety Code requires designated social media companies to comply with measures including minimising harmful content for children, community guidelines, safety tools, and detecting child sexual exploitation and abuse material and terrorism content, subject to penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Indeed, these are things that we can continue to review as we see what have been the efforts that are put in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But just to clarify, the Online Safety Code had already put in certain things that the designated social media companies need to comply with, and if they do not, they will be subject to penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These include putting in place systems and processes to minimise presence of harmful content in the services, particularly for children, and establishing community guidelines, enforcing them, providing users of access to tools to manage their own safety and proactively detecting and removing child sexual exploitation and abuse material, as well as terrorism content.

sections.label: Collaboration with technology companies
sections.summary: Singapore takes a collaborative but strict approach with technology companies, requiring compliance and safeguards through a continuous iterative process of annual reports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have had a very collaborative approach that we have taken with the technology companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have been very stern and strict in making sure that they comply with some of the requirements that we have set forth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With regard to the question on whether they have been putting in the necessary safeguards, I think this is the whole point of the exercise with the annual reports because it is going to be a continuous iterative process.
